coverage_limits: OpenAlex returned HTTP 429 after about six queries (shared rate limit), so citation chasing and reference-list expansion through OpenAlex were not done; the arXiv API was also rate-limited, so arXiv records were confirmed from arxiv.org abstract pages instead. SSRN pages return HTTP 403, so SSRN abstracts come from Crossref records or search snippets; for four SSRN items (Chen-Brandimarte-Susarla, Xiao-Chen-Liu, Alavi-Nozari, Cao et al.) no abstract was available and only the first two that were clearly relevant were kept with notes. The AEA registry bulk data sit behind a Dataverse guestbook that asks for personal details, so registry coverage relies on web search and individual trial pages and is incomplete. IDEAS and EconPapers search forms do not work through fetches, so RePEc coverage comes from NEP report listings (NEP-AIN complete since its start in June 2023; NEP-EXP and NEP-CUL from 2023; NEP-INO and NEP-ENT from mid-2024; NEP-CBE from 2024; NEP-BEC only through February 2026), filtered on AI terms in titles, and from title-only Crossref searches, which can miss productivity experiments whose titles do not mention creativity but that report originality sub-scores (Noy and Zhang was found this way only through a conference PDF). CESifo and CEPR websites were not searched directly. The ICML 2026 Workshop on Human-AI Co-Creativity (where Jo and Raghavan appeared) likely lists more relevant experiments but is outside this lane and was not scanned.

candidates.title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
candidates.task: occupation-specific professional writing tasks (reports, analysis plans, emails)
candidates.evidence: Preregistered online experiment randomly gave half of 453 college-educated professionals ChatGPT for incentivized writing tasks; blind graders' scores rose about 0.45 SD, with similar gains in the originality sub-grade (the paper states this in the conference draft). Creativity enters only as an originality sub-score of a productivity study.

candidates.title: How and for whom using generative AI affects creativity: A field experiment
candidates.task: workplace creativity tasks at a technology consulting firm
candidates.evidence: Field experiment randomly assigned employees of a technology consulting firm to ChatGPT (LLM) assistance or none; supervisor and external-evaluator creativity ratings rose with LLM assistance, mostly for employees high in metacognitive strategies. N=250 comes from university news coverage, not the abstract.

candidates.title: The Double-Edged Roles of Generative AI in the Creative Process: Experiments on Design Work
candidates.task: design ideation and implementation (students in lab; professional designers)
candidates.evidence: Controlled lab experiments with students and tests with professional designers compare GenAI-assisted with unassisted design work; GenAI raised rated creativity at the ideation stage for all users, while experts gained no creativity and lost time at implementation. Assignment method and N are not in the abstract.

candidates.title: Unlocking creativity with artificial intelligence (AI): Field and experimental evidence on the Goldilocks (curvilinear) effect of human–AI collaboration
candidates.task: entrepreneurial challenge with varying degrees of ChatGPT collaboration
candidates.evidence: Two experiments (139 business professionals, 319 working adults) assigned participants to collaborate with ChatGPT to different degrees on an entrepreneurial challenge; judge-rated creativity, entrepreneur-rated business value and AI-rated creativity peaked at moderate collaboration. A multiwave survey of 188 creative-industry workers is also reported (not counted in N).

candidates.title: Human-AI Interaction in Creative Tasks: an Experimental Investigation
candidates.venue: Working Papers, Department of Economics, Ca' Foscari University of Venice, No. 16/WP/2026
candidates.task: short creative composition ('If you had the talent to create something simply with your thoughts, what would you create?')
candidates.evidence: Lab experiment in Venice randomly assigned 360 participants to ChatGPT access or none, crossed with piece-rate, tournament and lottery incentives; external Prolific raters scored creativity. AI access raised scores only among participants who queried it, with a concave relation in the number of queries.

candidates.title: Help That Hurts: The Creativity Cost of Generative AI Ideation in Music Composition
other_versions: Poster at the Conference on Digital Experimentation (CODE@MIT), per CMU news, January 2026
candidates.task: compose an original 15-second piano melody, with or without Udio text-to-music ideation
candidates.evidence: RCT assigned musically trained participants to an AI-ideation group (Udio) or a no-AI control; external listeners rated melodies from the AI group as less creative, and AI access shifted stylistic choices. N=140 comes from a CMU news release; the abstract gives no N.

candidates.title: Training Novices to Think, or Giving Them LLMs? Evidence from an RCT
candidates.task: marketing recommendations for a university merchandise store (business case)
candidates.evidence: 2x2 RCT with 1,053 first-year Bocconi undergraduates crossed ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) access with causal-reasoning training. ChatGPT raised expert rubric scores and the number of ideas and made solutions more similar to expert texts, but left within- and between-solution idea diversity largely unchanged; reasoning training raised diversity.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.HC); ICML 2026 Workshop on Human-AI Co-Creativity
other_versions: ICML 2026 Workshop on Human-AI Co-Creativity, icml.cc/virtual/2026/68591
candidates.task: short story writing (250-350 words) with or without a GPT-5-mini assistant
candidates.evidence: Preregistered 2x2 RCT on Prolific (N=200) crossed AI assistant versus writing alone with originality-based versus quality-based incentives; collective diversity measured with embedding and n-gram similarity. Originality incentives made AI-assisted stories collectively more diverse, closer to the no-AI baselines.

candidates.title: Generative AI Enhances Team Performance and Reduces Need for Traditional Teams
candidates.task: team content-generation (articles) and innovation/strategy tasks
candidates.evidence: Preregistered experiment randomly assigned 435 participants in 122 teams to human-only, single-ChatGPT-4 or multiple-ChatGPT-4 teams (plus 139 individuals working with ChatGPT in a second experiment); blind judges rated overall quality, novelty and usefulness, all higher for AI-assisted teams.

candidates.title: Augmenting Minds or Automating Skills: The Differential Role of Human Capital in Generative AI's Impact on Creative Tasks
candidates.task: flash fiction writing; song lyric writing
candidates.evidence: Two randomized experiments assigned participants to GPT-4 assistance or no AI for flash fiction (Chinese) and lyric writing; online raters scored novelty and usefulness by consensual assessment. AI raised novelty and usefulness, more for high-IQ and educated participants and less for skilled writers. Exact Ns are not in the abstract (Experiment 2 began with 685 registrants).

candidates.title: More Ideas, Less Strategic Focus: How AI Changes the Alternatives Decision-Makers Consider
candidates.task: generating strategic alternatives for a business problem (MBA students)
candidates.evidence: RCT with 305 MBA students varied whether LLM support came during problem formulation or only during ideation and evaluation; LLM help increased the number of alternatives (fluency), and when given at problem formulation it reduced the strategic focus of the alternatives.

candidates.title: Harnessing GPT for Enhanced Academic Writing: Evidence from a Field Experiment with Early-Career Researchers in the Social Sciences
candidates.task: academic manuscript writing during a three-day hackathon
candidates.evidence: RCT with 22 early-career social scientists (with Springer Nature) randomized to unrestricted GPT-4 access or no AI; expert raters scored manuscripts on six dimensions including originality. AI improved clarity and coherence but not originality. Bibliographic record confirmed in Crossref; design and results come from a search snippet of the abstract because the SSRN page is blocked.

candidates.title: Human-AI Co-Creation in Product Ideation: the Dual View of Quality and Diversity
candidates.task: product ideation by humans, GPT-4 and human-GPT co-creation modes
candidates.evidence: Two online experiments compare human, GPT-4 and co-created product ideas (including human ideas revised with GPT); quality and diversity are measured by human evaluations and deep-learning assessments. GPT ideas were higher in quality but lower in diversity; human-first ideas with GPT revision balanced both.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Brainstorming: How Humans and Ai Beat Humans Alone
other_versions: doi 10.5465/amproc.2023.11938abstract (Academy of Management Proceedings 2023, 'AI-Augmented Creativity: Overcoming the Productivity Loss in Brainstorming Groups')
candidates.task: group brainstorming on a common question (nominal, interactive, hybrid human-AI, AI-only groups)
candidates.evidence: One-factor between-subjects lab experiment (N=168) compared nominal, interactive, hybrid human-AI and AI-only brainstorming groups on productivity and idea creativity; hybrid groups beat both human-only group types, and AI alone was the most efficient.

candidates.title: Elevating and Sharpening Convergent Thinking: The Potential of Generative AI for Creative Professionals
candidates.task: design ideation with text and images
candidates.evidence: Experiment compares human-only groups with human-GenAI groups on design ideation exercises using text and images, examining the quality and quantity of ideas in divergent and convergent phases; GenAI helped designers who ran short of ideas.

candidates.title: The Symbiotic Ceiling in Generative-AI-Assisted Design:,Measuring Creativity, Human Agency, and Cultural Specificity in Human-AI Interaction
candidates.task: design tasks with text-to-image tools under four AI-support conditions
candidates.evidence: Mixed-method experiment with 160 novice designers across four AI-support conditions; experts judged quality and originality, and similarity metrics captured visual diversity. Unstructured AI use gave more polish but lower originality and visual diversity than scaffolded use. Title copied as in the SSRN/Crossref record (stray comma).

candidates.title: The Double-Edged Sword of AI Hallucinations: Experimental Evidence on Creativity Across Idea Generation and Refinement
candidates.task: generating, selecting and refining patent-based product ideas with LLM assistance at manipulated hallucination levels
candidates.evidence: Experiment varied the hallucination level of LLM assistance; moderate and high hallucination raised originality, diversity and elaboration at idea generation, and raised originality at the cost of feasibility at refinement. SSRN lists the first author as 'Li Fanshu'; N not in abstract.

candidates.title: Does Increasing Reliance on Artificial Intelligence Boost Creativity? Assessing AI-Augmented Creativity with Large Language Models
other_versions: Chen, J. (2025) PhD dissertation 'Two Studies on Assessing AI-Augmented Creativity with Large Language Models', Michigan State University, d.lib.msu.edu/etd/52532
candidates.task: writing tasks with an LLM whose randomness is manipulated
candidates.evidence: No SSRN abstract was retrievable; the first author's dissertation describes a quasi-experiment that manipulated LLM randomness during human-LLM writing and found that high-randomness, more diverse advice did not necessarily raise the perceived creativity of the work.

candidates.title: Role Separation Beats Process Structure: An Experimental Comparison of AI-assisted Startup Ideation Methods
candidates.task: startup ideation in a university innovation workshop (four teams, 12 ideas)
candidates.evidence: Controlled quasi-experiment (16 participants in four teams) compared human-only ideation, unstructured AI use, a structured prompting framework, and that framework with separated AI roles; ideas were rated on problem-solution fit, market potential and feasibility (quality, not novelty).

candidates.title: The Effect of AI Support on Torrance's Creativity Dimensions: Evidence from an Online Experiment
candidates.venue: ECIS 2024 Proceedings (European Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.task: idea generation scored on Torrance dimensions
candidates.evidence: Online experiment (n=102) compared people working with AI support against people working alone; AI-supported ideas were more numerous, more elaborated and spread over more categories (fluency, elaboration, flexibility) but less original.

candidates.title: Assessment of the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Creative Storytelling for Enhancing the Ideation Process at the Individual Level
candidates.venue: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Creative Technologies 11(1)
candidates.task: Alternative Uses Test and creative storytelling
candidates.evidence: Ten polytechnic students split into two groups, one working with ChatGPT; ChatGPT raised fluency and flexibility and improved originality on Guilford's AUT but did not improve creative storytelling.

candidates.title: Enhancing designer creativity through human–AI co-ideation: a co-creation framework for design ideation with custom GPT
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing
candidates.task: industrial design ideation with a custom GPT (Co-Ideator) versus traditional ideation
candidates.evidence: Design case study compared ideation using a custom-GPT co-ideation framework with traditional ideation and a non-AI condition; co-ideation with the custom GPT gave higher novelty and quality of ideation. Assignment and N not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Scaffolding Creativity: How Divergent and Convergent LLM Personas Shape Human Machine Creative Problem-Solving
candidates.authors: Rosenbaum, David, Kaufman, Ravid, Ronen, Krebs
candidates.task: creative problem solving with a persona-based LLM coach
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment: participants worked with a divergent-thinking LLM persona, a convergent persona, or a standard answer-giving LLM (control); objective creativity performance was compared across conditions, and users' perceptions often diverged from it. N not in abstract.

candidates.title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
candidates.task: executing NLP research ideas (LLM-generated versus expert-written)
candidates.evidence: 43 expert researchers were randomly assigned to execute an LLM-generated or an expert-written research idea (over 100 hours each); blind reviewers scored projects on novelty, excitement, effectiveness and overall. LLM ideas lost more after execution, closing the ideation-stage novelty gap. Follow-up to Si et al., already collected.

candidates.title: A comment on 'An Empirical Investigation of the Impact of ChatGPT on Creativity'
candidates.task: computational reproduction of Lee and Chung (2024) ChatGPT creativity RCTs
candidates.evidence: Institute for Replication report reproduces all main results of Lee and Chung's six RCTs (ChatGPT versus web search versus no help on creative ideas) from original data and code, notes minor coding errors, and adds a robustness check: response time is unrelated to rated creativity in the ChatGPT arm. No new data.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence and Human Creativity
candidates.task: assembling a matchstick figure in five minutes (adults and children)
candidates.evidence: Trial registration only (status 'in development'; no linked paper): no assistance versus generative-AI assistance with preselected or free prompts; a judging panel rates originality and elaboration. Planned 50-70 adults and 50-70 children per arm.

candidates.title: Incentives for Creative Production: Assessing the Marginal Contribution of Artificial Intelligence
candidates.task: written creative tasks with and without AI under fixed, piece-rate and tournament pay
candidates.evidence: Trial registration only (no paper listed): within-subject writing without and with AI help across three incentive arms; scores for originality, grammar and engagement, plus share of AI text used. Planned 360 participants.

candidates.title: The effect of Generative AI on Early Stage Business Ideas: An Experimental Approach
candidates.task: early-stage business idea development by engineering student teams
candidates.evidence: Trial registration only (no paper listed): group-level randomization (at least 130 teams) of guidance on using AI for early-stage idea development; outcomes are judges' grades of problem relevance and value proposition plus venture outcomes, with no explicit novelty measure. Kept because the stated aim is discovery of novel business ideas.

candidates.title: The Effect of AI on Idea Generation and Evaluation
candidates.task: business idea generation and evaluation
candidates.evidence: Trial registration (status completed; no linked paper found): participants randomly assigned to ChatGPT-assisted or independent idea generation, after which all generate and evaluate ideas without AI; outcomes include number, speed and quality of ideas. Planned 200 participants.

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Research Productivity
candidates.task: writing research proposals with and without AI
candidates.evidence: Trial registration only (in development): three rounds of research-proposal writing with AI permitted for treatment groups only; outcomes include expert ratings, and 'methodological novelty' and 'innovativeness' scores are listed as to be determined. Planned 400 participants. Weak fit; kept for the possible novelty outcome.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence and its impact on creativity and diversity: An empirical study of large language model-generated product ideas
candidates.authors: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich
candidates.task: new product ideas for college students priced under $50
candidates.evidence: Series of studies comparing LLM-generated with human (student) product ideas: LLM ideas had higher purchase-intent quality but were less novel and less diverse at the set level; re-analysis of prior LLM creativity studies and tests of prompting, model pooling and agents to restore diversity. Consolidates Girotra et al. (2023) and Meincke et al. (2024), both already collected.

candidates.title: Examining and Addressing Barriers to Diversity in LLM-Generated Ideas
candidates.task: idea generation by independent human samples versus independent LLM samples
candidates.evidence: Four studies compare the diversity of ideas from independent humans and independent LLM samples, trace low LLM diversity to fixation and to the absence of knowledge partitioning, and show that chain-of-thought prompting plus ordinary personas raise LLM idea diversity above human levels.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligences and Human Scientists Exhibit Complementary Strengths in Theory Building
candidates.task: theory formulation, novel predictions and theory revision on gender and race inequality
candidates.evidence: Compares 25 LLMs with 13 senior researchers and 60 doctoral scholars: AIs beat most humans individually and their theories were rated higher quality by blind raters, but human theories were more diverse and gained more predictive accuracy from aggregation.

candidates.title: AI-AI co-creation outperforms human pairs in creative tasks
candidates.task: three open-ended ideation tasks (1,212 ideas rated)
candidates.evidence: Experiment compares AI-AI co-creation (complementary or identical roles), single-AI creation and human-human pairs; trained judges rated 1,212 ideas on creativity, novelty and usefulness, and both AI-AI conditions beat single AI and human pairs on creativity and novelty. No person received AI help.

candidates.title: Comparing the Ideation Quality of Humans With Generative Artificial Intelligence
candidates.task: new product and service ideas from professionals versus an AI system
candidates.evidence: Blind expert evaluation of ideas from human professionals and from an AI system: AI ideas scored higher on novelty and customer benefit, similar on feasibility, and made up most of the top ideas.

candidates.title: Pron vs Prompt: Can Large Language Models already Challenge a World-Class Fiction Author at Creative Text Writing?
candidates.authors: Marco, Gonzalo, Mateo-Girona, Del Castillo Santos
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pp. 19654-19670
candidates.task: short-story titles and stories by novelist Patricio Pron versus GPT-4
candidates.evidence: Contest in which Pron and GPT-4 each wrote 30 titles and stories for both sets of titles; literary critics and scholars gave 5,400 rubric assessments based on Boden's creativity criteria; GPT-4 fell well short of the top human writer, though it wrote more creatively from Pron's titles.

candidates.title: Are Semantic Networks Associated with Idea Originality in Artificial Creativity? A Comparison with Human Agents
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: standardized creativity and semantic-network tests
candidates.evidence: Administers standardized tests to ChatGPT-4o and 81 psychology students split into higher and lower creative groups; ChatGPT-4o had a more rigid semantic network but was more original than lower-creative humans.

candidates.title: The paradox of creativity in generative AI: high performance, human-like bias, and limited differential evaluation
candidates.task: egg task (fixation bias and original idea generation)
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-4o's egg-task ideas are compared with 47 human participants and with pooled data from eight earlier studies; ChatGPT was more productive but showed a similar fixation bias and could not tell original from conventional ideas.

candidates.title: Echoes in AI: Quantifying lack of plot diversity in LLM outputs
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 122(35), e2504966122
candidates.task: story generation by GPT-4 and LLaMA-3 versus human-written stories
candidates.evidence: Introduces a Sui Generis score of plot-element uniqueness; LLM stories reuse plot elements across generations and models, while plots from human-written stories are rarely echoed, so human plots are far more diverse.

candidates.title: How Creative Is AI Writing? Generative and Collaborative AI in Japanese Fiction
other_versions: doi 10.5210/spir.v2024i0.15341 (AoIR Selected Papers of Internet Research)
candidates.task: endings of Japanese literary fiction: human, zero-shot AI, detailed-prompt AI, human-AI collaboration
candidates.evidence: 58 readers with creative-writing backgrounds ranked story endings across four conditions; human-AI collaboration ranked highest in quality but lowest in originality, and the authors read GenAI's contribution as a reduction of variance. N counts raters, not writers.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence and Strategic Decision-Making: Evidence from Entrepreneurs and Investors
candidates.task: generating and evaluating startup strategies (accelerator program; start-up competition)
candidates.evidence: Evidence from an accelerator program and a start-up competition that LLMs generate and evaluate strategies at a level comparable to entrepreneurs and investors. Weak fit: strategy quality rather than novelty or diversity, and mostly a conceptual paper.

candidates.title: Psittacines of Innovation? Assessing the True Novelty of AI Creations
candidates.task: project titles for hypothetical crowdfunding campaigns versus real campaign titles
candidates.evidence: Compares AI-generated crowdfunding project titles with observed field titles using maximum mean discrepancy on embeddings, plus within-AI repetition; AI output diverges from field data. Borderline model-only: the human side is field data, with no human raters or participants.

candidates.title: The Ideation Bottleneck: Decomposing the Quality Gap Between AI-Generated and Human Economics Research
candidates.task: economics research papers (912 AI-generated versus 41 published human papers)
candidates.evidence: Compares idea quality and execution quality of AI-generated and human economics papers using fine-tuned models and an LLM rubric; the idea-quality gap is large. Borderline: idea quality is scored by models, not human raters, and is not a novelty measure.

candidates.title: Generative AI and the Homogenization of Brand Identity: Why AI-generated Brands Struggle to Feel Original, and Why It Matters for the Future of Design
candidates.task: brand identities (logo, palette, tagline) generated by AI versus real brands
candidates.evidence: Tests whether AI-generated brand identities converge across unrelated products and compares real and AI-generated brands on UEQ dimensions including novelty. Low methodological detail in the abstract.

candidates.title: Does ChatGPT Help You Sell More? Effects of Large Language Models on Review Homogeneity and Product Sales
candidates.task: Amazon product reviews (about 5 million Electronics reviews, plus Books) and AI versus human reviews
candidates.evidence: Study 1 shows AI-generated reviews are semantically more homogeneous than human reviews; Study 2 uses a year-over-year difference-in-differences on Amazon reviews (2021-2023) and finds review homogeneity rose after ChatGPT's release; Study 3 links homogeneity to sales.

candidates.title: Does Generative AI Make Startup Ideas Alike? Evidence from Product Hunt
candidates.task: 291,314 Product Hunt launches, January 2018 to April 2026
candidates.evidence: After ChatGPT's release, launches concentrate around common category concepts and the share of distinctive launches falls from 25% to 16%; the rise in similarity is larger where LLMs can better assist ideation, and holds within first-time and experienced teams.

candidates.title: A Dual Pathway Model of How Generative AI Use Shapes Creative Outcomes: Empirical Evidence from Human Representations in Artworks
candidates.task: 6,812,452 artworks on a large art-sharing platform
candidates.evidence: Staggered difference-in-differences comparing creators who start using generative AI with non-users: GenAI use widened the diversity of facial representations but reduced demographic diversity (age, gender, race) in artworks; mechanisms tested in computational and human-subject experiments.

candidates.title: Spillover Effects of Generative AI on Human-Generated Content Creation: Evidence from a Crowd-Sourcing Design Platform
candidates.task: organic (non-AI) designs on an online crowdsourcing design platform after designers adopt generative AI
candidates.evidence: Econometric analysis of platform data on how adopting generative AI changes the novelty of designers' own human-made designs; initial reliance suppressed novelty but longer use raised it, most for designers with both AI and domain expertise.

candidates.title: Does Generative AI Crowd Out Human Creators? Evidence from Pixiv
candidates.task: illustration and comic posts on Pixiv after a text-to-image AI launch
candidates.evidence: Incumbent illustrators who do not adopt AI cut uploads after the launch; those more exposed to AI-generated content avoid AI-favored tags and broaden the range of IPs they draw, a content-diversification response. Weak fit: diversity of non-adopters' output, not of AI-assisted output.

candidates.title: Bridging Language Barriers: The Impact of Large Language Models on Academic Writing
candidates.task: over one million arXiv abstracts by native and nonnative English speakers
candidates.evidence: Before-after ChatGPT analysis of lexical diversity and readability shows the writing of native and nonnative speakers converged in lexical diversity, with the largest gains for nonnative authors.

candidates.title: The Behavioral Signature of GenAI in Scientific Communication
candidates.task: IZA discussion paper abstracts before and after ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Event-study on IZA DP abstracts finds an abrupt stylistic shift after ChatGPT-3.5 (word length, type-token ratio, readability) and growing similarity to GPT-optimized versions, read as convergence toward machine-style writing.

candidates.title: Divergent LLM Adoption and Heterogeneous Convergence Paths in Research Writing
candidates.task: over 627,000 arXiv papers
candidates.evidence: Detects ChatGPT-revised style with fine-tuned classifiers and, in a difference-in-differences analysis, finds that LLM use drives convergence in academic writing, strongest for early adopters, male, nonnative and junior researchers.

candidates.title: Research Novelty in Information Systems Journals After ChatGPT: Differences Across Institutional Language Contexts
candidates.task: 13,847 articles in 44 Information Systems journals, 2020-2025
candidates.evidence: Measures each article's semantic distance from recent predecessors (SPECTER2) and finds a 0.176 SD larger post-2022 decline in relative novelty for first authors in non-English-dominant countries; LLM use itself is not observed. alphaXiv lists the paper as 'Do Large Language Models Reduce Research Novelty? Evidence from Information Systems Journals', likely an earlier version title.

candidates.title: The Impact of Large Language Models on Open-source Innovation: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
candidates.task: open-source software contributions after GitHub Copilot
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experimental analysis of open-source contributions finds Copilot raised contributions by 28-40%, with much larger growth in incremental than in substantive (new-functionality) contributions, tilting innovation toward exploitation. Weak fit: novelty-type outcome in code, not a creativity rating.

candidates.title: Generative AI-Style Analyst Writing, Narrative Convergence, and Market Response
candidates.task: 93,055 Korean sell-side analyst reports, 2015-2025
candidates.evidence: Reports on the same firm event are more similar in semantic content and structure when covering analysts have higher prior exposure to AI-style writing, alongside stronger trading responses. Author is Hojun Kim (distinct from Ho Kim above).

candidates.title: AI Product Review Summaries and Content Homogenization: The Changing Landscape of UGC
candidates.task: user-generated product reviews after AI-generated review summaries
candidates.evidence: Only title and authors could be confirmed (no abstract in Crossref; SSRN blocked; no search snippet). The title indicates a study of homogenization of user-generated reviews linked to AI review summaries; kept for recall and needs checking.

candidates.title: Creative Minds in the Age of AI. Personality Traits, AI Perception, and Creativity Tasks
candidates.task: Divergent Association Task, Alternative Uses Task and a constrained narrative task
candidates.evidence: Survey of 260 participants on AI use and attitudes plus creativity tasks; creativity is highest with reflective, moderate AI engagement and lower with minimal or heavy reliance. Correlational, with no AI assignment; possibly relevant to after_ai as a cross-sectional link between AI habits and unassisted creativity.

candidates.title: Generative artificial intelligence in creative contexts: a systematic review and future research agenda
candidates.task: systematic literature review of 64 studies on GenAI in creative contexts
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of 64 studies on methods, trends and themes of GenAI in creative contexts, including implications for creative outcomes; no meta-analysis.

candidates.title: Generative AI Use in Entrepreneurship: An Integrative Review and an Empowerment-Entrapment Framework
candidates.task: integrative review of GenAI across stages of entrepreneurship, including ideation
candidates.evidence: Integrative (not systematic) review of how GenAI affects entrepreneurs from opportunity recognition and ideation onward, including idea-quality gains and costs; cites Product Hunt evidence on startup-idea similarity. Weak fit.

candidates.title: Why Premium AI Subscriptions Don't Transform Mediocrity Into Genius: Empirical Evidence on the Creativity Gap in Human-AI Collaboration
candidates.task: narrative synthesis of 2025 studies on AI-assisted creativity
candidates.evidence: Narrative synthesis of other studies (a 442-person study and a 28-study meta-analysis) arguing that AI amplifies baseline creative ability and reduces idea diversity; no original data and not a systematic review. Low priority.

candidates.title: Assimilating generative AI into ideation work: seeding, search and human contribution
candidates.task: ideation by professionals under four configurations (human-only, unstructured human-GenAI, GenAI seeding, TC-based GenAI seeding)
candidates.evidence: Tests four ideation configurations with 400 professionals; expert evaluators rate novelty, utility and feasibility. Unstructured GenAI collaboration and plain GenAI seeding gave no reliable gains over human-only ideation; a TC-based GenAI configuration raised novelty but lowered feasibility. Assignment method not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Ideation and the performance of Innovation Teams (Preprint)
candidates.task: team ideation: healthcare product/service for older people and automotive business model innovation
candidates.evidence: Framed field experiment with three-person teams using a custom GenAI ideation tool versus a control group; AI teams produced higher-quality ideas (originality, clarity, completeness) faster and with more idea diversity. N=70 and the description 'randomized' come from the Mendeley dataset page; the arXiv abstract gives neither.

candidates.title: Asymmetric Discourse Homogenization and Shared Language Technology: Evidence from Reddit
candidates.task: 6 million Reddit comments in cross-partisan political forums, 2019-2025
candidates.evidence: Tracks semantic similarity of political discourse against a cumulative LLM-exposure index; finds an ideologically asymmetric break in the diversification trend around late 2022 (less diversity among conservative users), which the author reads as community-level convergence rather than individual AI adoption.

candidates.title: Are Scientists Starting to Sound like ChatGPT? Stylistic Diffusion in Biomedical Abstracts in the LLM Era
candidates.task: 28,415 PubMed abstracts, 2018-2025
candidates.evidence: Interrupted time-series analysis of LLM-associated stylistic markers, lexical diversity and semantic similarity in biomedical abstracts finds a post-ChatGPT 'same-ification' style shift (marker use up 133%). Diversity results beyond markers are not detailed in the abstract.

candidates.title: Has AI Surpassed Humans in Creative Idea Generation? A Meta-Analysis
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Annual Conference of the European Association of Cognitive Ergonomics (ECCE 2025)
other_versions: MIC 2025 conference abstract 'Generative AI has not (yet?) surpassed humans in creative idea generation: A meta-analysis (2022-2025)'
candidates.task: meta-analysis of 17 experiments (115 effect sizes) comparing human and GenAI-prompted idea generation
candidates.evidence: Published proceedings version of de Rooij (2025), already collected; reported here only to link the ACM DOI. Pooled effect favoring GenAI is small and non-significant; apparent originality advantage driven by a few studies.

candidates.title: Human-GenAI Dynamics in Problem-Finding and Idea Generation
candidates.venue: Doctoral thesis, City St George's, University of London
candidates.task: consumer product ideation under input-resource and financial constraints
candidates.evidence: Three-paper thesis; the second paper compares GenAI-assisted and human-only product ideation and reports that giving idea generation to GenAI and exploration to humans improves appropriateness with a marginal novelty gain. Full text embargoed until 2028; design details unconfirmed. Related published experiment: Sabbah, Banerjee, Li (2026), Information Technology & People, listed separately.
